_: The audio pipeline's one table: what to cut, from what, to what.
`npm run audio` reads this, cuts each master with ffmpeg and writes the
encoded file beside it; `npm run build` refuses a stale or over-budget
one through scripts/check-audio.mjs. See docs/audio.md for the argument.
EVERY NUMBER HERE IS THE INPUT, not a record of what happened. The cut
lives in `trim` rather than in a binary somebody has to open, so the
shipped file is reproducible from a committed master and a reviewable
diff. `sourceHash` and `decoded` are the only fields the generator
writes back, and they are what the build gate checks.
The ceiling, in the unit that actually binds. A decoded AudioBuffer is
duration * ctx.sampleRate * channels * 4 bytes and NOTHING else -- the
container, the bitrate and the file's own sample rate are invisible to
it (measured: a 22 kHz file decodes back up to 48 kHz for identical
RAM). So the budget is seconds of mono, not bytes on disk.
44 s = 8 MB at 48 kHz, ~5% of the 157 MB heap FINDINGS.md #1 measures.
A stereo row spends two seconds of it per second of audio.
Cut to the REPORT and nothing after it. The master carries ~865 ms of
baked room -- a flat -18 to -24 dB plateau to 385 ms and then a slow
decay to -68 -- and Sfx already answers every gunshot with a shared
ConvolverNode on a send. Shipping the baked tail would double-reverb
the shot, put one fixed room on six maps, defeat botShot's
distance-climbing send, and hold a voice for 865 ms instead of 150.
Measured before cutting: the report's energy is gone by 130 ms (-8 dB
at 125, -20 by 135), and the 130-400 ms band has a crest factor of
6 dB with no window 5 dB above it -- dense noise, no discrete
reflection and no mechanism, so there is nothing in there to lose.
Stereo, which is the exception to the mono rule rather than a lapse:
the master carries real width (the side channel peaks 10.8 dB under
the mid, so it is not dual-mono), this is the one sample the player
hears UNPANNED as their own report, and at a 150 ms cut the second
channel costs 28 KB. The mono rule earns its keep on long sounds and
on anything only ever heard through a panner.
The only master here that is not one shot. A BURST weapon was recorded
as a burst: the second round arrives at 216 ms at -4 dB and a third
rides its tail out to ~330. `Sfx.shoot` is called once per ROUND, so a
sample carrying the burst would fire nine shots for every three -- this
is cut to the FIRST round and the rest is discarded as a matter of
correctness rather than of taste.
It is also the only master with a LEAD. The report's onset is at 32 ms
and everything before it is -23 to -41 dB of pre-noise; shipped whole
that is 32 ms of latency between the trigger and the sound, which on a
weapon whose three rounds leave 50 ms apart is a third of the burst.
The start sits in the trough at 24 ms (-41 dB) rather than hard against
the onset, so the cut needs no fade in to keep from clicking and the
transient keeps a foot.
96 ms, the shortest cut in the table, and the rate is why: `report.
length` is 0.75 for the same reason ("three of these leave in 0.1 s,
and at the rifle's own length they would run together into a single
ugly shout"). The direct sound is over at 98 ms anyway -- broadband
-9 dB at 96 and -19 by 100.
Cut in the trough between the shot and a discrete second arrival. The
report's high band decays from 124 ms and is 40 dB down by 144; then at
152-172 ms something HF-rich comes back at -8 dB in the band and -15
broadband, which is either a hard slapback or the bolt, and neither
belongs in a sample. `Sfx` answers the first with its own convolver and
the second with `actionPitch`/`actionVol` -- and this weapon's
`actionVol` is 1.55, the highest in the kit, because a blowback SMG is
mostly the sound of its own bolt. Shipping the recorded one would play
that mechanism twice.
140 ms against a 77 ms gap at 13 rounds a second, so two rounds always
overlap -- the same ratio the rifle already ships (150 ms on a 106 ms
gap), and the fade lands on the cliff rather than on the next round.
The longest cut in the table, and the master earns it rather than the
weapon being indulged: the high band stays live -- between -9 and -20 dB
-- all the way to 156 ms, drops to -26 at 160 and PLATEAUS there for the
next 60. A plateau in the high band is a room's early field; a decay is
a shot. So the direct sound genuinely runs to ~158 and the fade covers
the handover exactly.
What is discarded past it is that plateau out to 220 ms and then a
discrete late arrival at 224-232 (-10 dB broadband, 30 dB down in the
high band) -- a reflection off something a good way off, and the single
clearest case in these six of a room that is not this game's. At 3
rounds a second 180 ms is barely half the gap, so nothing here is
spent against the next round.
The one master with NO cliff in it, which is why this row's fade is
nearly a third of its length instead of the 15 ms every other row uses.
The rifle's cut could land on a 15 dB step at 130 ms and hide there;
this file is still only 6 dB down at 296 ms and its decay does not
become a straight line in dB until ~400. There is no moment to cut on,
so the cut has to be MADE, and a fade is the honest way to make one.
Where it goes is the high band. The crack is over by ~90 ms; from 95 ms
the band sits at -21 dB +/-2 for the next hundred milliseconds, which is
a dense early field rather than anything the weapon did, and at 200-212
a discrete arrival comes back at -9. So the shot is 0-90 and the fade
spends 90-130 handing it to `Sfx`'s convolver.
It is also the widest master in the set -- the side channel peaks only
3.8 dB under the mid, against the assault rifle's 10.8 -- which is the
room again, and another reason not to ship much of it: one recorded
room heard in stereo is the same fixed room on six maps that the
assault rifle's row argues against, only more audibly.
The second master with a lead, and the longest: 50 ms of it, -27 to
-57 dB, before the report starts at 52. Same rule as the burst rifle --
shipped whole it is 50 ms of trigger latency on a weapon that fires
every 100 -- and the same placement, in the trough at 40 ms (-50 dB)
rather than hard against the onset.
The end is where the high band stops decaying and the low band does
not. Above 4 kHz the shot falls from -7 dB at 116 ms to -33 at 140 and
-55 by 180, a clean exponential decay; broadband it is still -13 at 180
because what is left is low roll, and the 300-500 ms band measures a
crest factor of 2.6 to 3.8 dB, which is undiluted noise. That low roll
is exactly what `report.weight` and `length` are for, so the cut takes
the direct sound to ~140 and fades the rest out over the next 30.
The cleanest of the six and the closest in shape to the assault rifle's:
a report to ~100 ms and then a 20 dB collapse over the next 25. The one
thing inside it worth naming is the high-band spike at 84-92 ms, which
is the slide -- kept, because it is inside the report and the assault
rifle's own cut keeps the same event at 126 ms, and because the fade is
already running by the time it would have to be argued about.
What is dropped is a floor at -28 to -38 dB from 130 ms and then a late
arrival at 220-240 that climbs back to -21, which is the room.
The cupola gun on all three hulls, and the FIRST MONO ROW in this table.
Every other row is stereo under the exception docs/audio.md grants a
short sound the player hears UNPANNED as their own report; this one has
no such claim. `Game.resolveMg` reaches `Sfx.botShot` and not `shoot`,
deliberately -- the gun is twelve metres from the listener in a chase
view -- so a PannerNode makes the stereo and a second channel would be
double the RAM for nothing. It costs 0.112 mono-seconds where a stereo
cut of the same length would cost 0.224.
The THIRD master to lead with its mechanism, and the plainest of them: a
discrete clack at 8-16 ms (-6 dB in the band above 4 kHz), then near
silence to -61, then the report at 40. Cut at 34 ms, in that trough. The
clack is a feed or a bolt and `actionPitch`/`actionVol` on the three mg
rows are what voice it, as on every other row here.
The end is the rate. The report is over at ~126 ms -- broadband -11 at
124 and -19 by 128, with the band above 4 kHz decaying from -21 -- and
what follows is low roll the room is holding, at -10 to -18 broadband
with that band 24 to 36 dB down, plus a discrete arrival at 148. The cut
is 112 ms, which is the tank's own 111 ms gap at fireRate 9 to within a
millisecond: one round is done when the next one leaves, no two stack,
and that is the same claim `report.length` of 0.72 already makes for this
gun ("almost no ring, because the next one is 110 ms away"). The truck's
133 ms and the helicopter's 118 are looser still.
The magazine stripped out of the well, and the FIRST OF TWO ROWS CUT FROM
ONE MASTER -- `src/reload.wav` is a performance rather than an event, and
the two moments in it that the game has a beat for are 2.4 s apart.
It is also the first row here that is not a REPORT. The rule it has to
pass is the one docs/audio.md sets for every file in this directory and
not a new one: the game is still whole with `audio/` deleted, because
`Sfx.reload` falls through to the clack it always played. What it may not
do is what a footstep library would -- see that file's arithmetic. Two
cuts, 0.436 mono-seconds, one master, no round robin.
The master is GATED to digital silence between gestures, which is why
there is no room to fight here and no 850 ms tail to discard. What it
holds is: the removal at 24-330 ms, silence to 1948, three small handling
noises (the fresh magazine coming up out of a pouch) to 2668, and the
insertion at 2714-3000. This row is the second half of the removal and
`magIn` is the insertion; everything else is the 2.4 s of fetching that
`CONFIG.viewmodel.reload` spends between `magOut` and `insertFrom`, and
no weapon's reload is the length this take was.
The removal is itself two gestures 140 ms apart, with a trough at -65 to
-71 dB between them: 24-135 ms is the catch pressed and the magazine
rocking loose, and 175-330 is it stripped clear -- a rattle to 194, a
scrape plateau at -32 to 230, and the magazine coming free at 0 dBFS at
249. Only the second is here. The first is CUT for the reason the
carbine's 32 ms lead is: `Sfx.reload`'s beats are FRACTIONS of the
weapon's `reloadTime` and a recorded pair is a fixed 140 ms apart, so
shipped together they agree only at one reload speed and drift 390 ms
apart on the LMG. The catch is beat 0 and is still the synthesized clack
it always was; this row is beat `magOut` and nothing else. What a sample
may contain is ONE BEAT's worth of sound, which is the burst rifle's rule
one level down.
The start is in the trough at 172 (-67 dB) rather than against the 175 ms
onset, so the cut cannot click and the transient keeps a foot. The end is
the decay reaching the master's own noise floor: broadband -15 dB at 254
falling to -72 at 330 with the band above 4 kHz tracking it down -22 to
-78, monotone the whole way. A DECAY and not a plateau, by the same test
that placed the seven reports, so there is no early field in here to hand
to the convolver -- the gate already took it.
MONO, and for a different reason than `mountedGun`'s. That row is mono
because of where it is heard; this one is heard exactly where the stereo
exception applies -- unpanned, the player's own -- and is mono because
there is no width in the master to keep. The side channel peaks 21.6 dB
under the mid and its RMS 22 dB under, against the assault rifle's 10.8
and the sniper's 3.8. That is dual-mono with a room mic's worth of drift
on it. The exception is for width that EXISTS.
The fresh magazine rocked into the well and slapped home -- the second cut
from `src/reload.wav`, and the only row in this table with a deliberate
PRE-ROLL in front of its transient.
Every other row is scheduled by its start, because a report's transient IS
its start. This one is an ARRIVAL: 193 ms of the magazine coming up and
being rocked nose-first into the well (the onset at 2718, a second hit at
2792, a rattle through 2848-2892) and then the seat itself at -0.1 dBFS at
2905. `CONFIG.viewmodel.reload` draws exactly that -- `insertFrom` to
`magSeat` is the magazine rising WITH the hand and `seatKick` is the
weapon taking the slap -- so `Sfx.reload` schedules this row by its PEAK
and lets the approach run ahead of the beat, which is what makes the
recorded gesture land on the drawn one. The peak offsets are the two
numbers in `Sfx` that are measured off these trims, and moving a `start`
here without moving one there slides the sound off the picture.
The pre-roll fits every weapon in the kit with room to spare: the tightest
is the sidearm, whose `magSeat` is 578 ms into a 1.05 s reload against
193/1.25 = 155 ms of approach.
Cut at 2712, six milliseconds of the master's -85 dB floor ahead of the
onset. The end is where the decay passes `Sfx`'s own SAMPLE_FLOOR: 70 dB
of monotone fall from the seat, high band tracking broadband down to -70,
reaching -54 dBFS peak at ~2982 -- which is the level `trimSample` calls
silence, so anything past it would be cut on decode anyway. The 20 ms fade
lands there rather than on the master's own hard end at 3.000.
Mono, for the reason in `magOut`'s note: the side channel is 21.6 dB under
the mid here too.
The handle turned up out of its notch, and the FIRST OF FOUR ROWS CUT FROM
ONE MASTER -- `src/bolt-cycle.wav` is the second performance in this
directory and the first that is a whole GESTURE rather than two moments with
a fetch between them. `Sfx.boltCycle` places its beats as fractions of
`weapons.sniper.shotInterval`; the take holds four of them and each one is
its own row, for the reason `magOut` states: what a sample may contain is
ONE BEAT's worth of sound. Shipped whole, a 3.0 s recording of somebody
working a bolt agrees with the drawn gesture at exactly one rate and at no
other, and `fireRate: 0.8` is a number that gets tuned.
The master is four gestures in two pairs: the handle lifted (12-292 ms) and
the bolt drawn to its stop (476-688), then 1.86 s of the action held OPEN,
then it driven home (2548-2750) and the handle turned down (2820-2960).
That is the game's `lift`, `back`, `home` and `lock` in the order it draws
them, which is why there are four rows and not one and not seven.
This row is the first pair's first half. What is in it: a bed of the firing
hand arriving on the knob at -30 to -46 dB, the handle camming up at 79 and
99 ms, the lugs breaking free at 0 dBFS at 165, and the bolt taking its
first movement to the rear at 224. It runs 41% of the cut past its own peak
on purpose -- `[lift, back]` is drawn as the bolt being drawn, and the
recorded gesture spilling into it is the wait being made audible, which is
what the two synthesized SLIDES were for and what they hand over to here.
**It is the tightest of the four in front, and that is what set its start.**
Every row here is scheduled by its PEAK (see `magIn` for why an arrival is),
so the approach in front of the transient has to fit inside the beat:
`peak / actionPitch` against `0.16 * shotInterval`, which is the SHORTEST
window in the gesture. Cut at the master's own 12 ms onset the approach is
153 ms against 200 available at the sniper's 0.68 and 0.8/s -- 9 ms of room,
and a fireRate raised at all would clamp it and put the lugs late. Cut here
it is 160 ms, which holds to 1.0/s. What is dropped is a discrete tick at
19 ms and 15 ms of the bed under it; the start is in the trough at 56 ms
(-46 dB, the deepest between that tick and the first hit) rather than hard
against an onset, which is the rule the three reports with a lead follow.
MONO, for `magOut`'s reason rather than `mountedGun`'s: this is heard
exactly where the stereo exception applies -- unpanned, the player's own,
`Sfx.boltCycle` takes no panner -- and there is no width in the master to
keep. The side channel peaks 15.2 dB under the mid on this cut and its RMS
16.1 dB under (the four rows run 13.7 to 23.3 dB peak and 15.9 to 19.6 RMS),
against the assault rifle's 10.8 and the sniper report's 3.8. The exception
is for width that EXISTS, and four stereo rows would cost 1.616
mono-seconds instead of 0.808 for a difference nothing can hear.
The bolt drawn to the rear stop with the case coming clear -- the second
cut, and the one that carries TWO of the synthesis's beats rather than one.
`Sfx.boltCycle` places the stop at 0.42 and the case at 0.47, 62 ms apart on
the sniper, because a synthesized stop cannot also be a piece of brass. On
the tape they are one event: 115 ms of the bolt travelling (-13 to -40 dB,
brightening as the action opens to the air) and then the stop at -0.2 dBFS
at 597, whose spectrum is 46% above 8 kHz against 18% at the bolt going home
and 30% either side of it here. That is the brass, and it is in the same
millisecond as the steel. So this row replaces the stop, the case AND the
opening slide, which is the SMG's rule (its `actionVol` of 1.55 is why that
master's own bolt was cut off the back) read the other way round: a
mechanism must not be played twice, whichever half of it is the recording.
Start at 476 in the master's floor (-77 dB at the cut, the onset at 479);
end where the ring passes `Sfx`'s own SAMPLE_FLOOR -- monotone from -0.2 at
597 to -52 by 656 with no plateau anywhere in it, which is the test that
placed the eight reports and says this recording is DRY. The 30 ms fade
lands on that decay.
**The master is NOT gated, which is the one way it differs from
`reload.wav`.** Its floor between gestures is a real preamp tone at -72 dB
RMS and -55 to -59 dB peak, where `reload.wav`'s is -90. It changes nothing:
the floor is under `trimSample`'s -54 dBFS, so the head of every one of
these four is measured off rather than played, and 55 to 63 dB of monotone
decay with no plateau is a dry recording with noise under it and not a room.
There is still nothing in here to hand to the convolver.
The bolt driven forward onto a round and closed -- the third cut, the far
side of the 1.86 s the action spends open, and the loudest arrival in the
take (0 dBFS at 2680).
It carries the closing SLIDE with it for the same reason `boltBack` carries
the opening one: 133 ms of the bolt running forward over the magazine ahead
of the peak -- six discrete contacts at -4 to -20 dB, which is a round being
stripped and is not something a filtered noise sweep was ever going to say.
The pair of synthesized slides they replace swept in OPPOSITE directions on
purpose (see `Sfx.boltCycle`), and the recorded pair does the same thing for
free: the opening one brightens to 46% above 8 kHz at the stop and this one
arrives at a centroid of 5.1 kHz against that stop's 7.5, because it ends on
a locked breech and not on air.
Cut at 2544 in the floor (-67 dB), 12 ms ahead of the onset at 2556, and
ended at 2758 where the decay has passed -60. 214 ms is the longest of the
four and the master earns it: at the sniper's `actionPitch` of 0.68 it plays
for 272 and covers 654-926 ms of a 1250 ms cycle, which with the other three
leaves ONE 22 ms gap in the whole gesture -- and that gap is the bolt sitting
at the rear stop, which is the one moment in a bolt cycle that is silent.
The handle turned down into its notch: the sound that says the weapon is
live again, and the one the player has spent a second and a quarter waiting
on. The shortest of the four at 148 ms and the brightest thing in the master
-- 62% of its peak's energy above 8 kHz and a centroid of 9.9 kHz against
the closing bolt's 5.1 -- which is a wrist turning a small piece of steel
into a recess rather than a mass being stopped, and is why
`CONFIG.viewmodel.cycle` gives `lock` no impulse where `back` and `home`
each get one.
Cut at 2814 in the floor (-79 dB) with the onset at 2820: 84 ms of the hand
coming down ahead of the click at 2903, then the ring out to -55 by 2950.
The 30 ms fade covers that ring rather than the master's own hard end at
3.000, and what is past it is floor.
It is the LAST sound of the gesture and it has to be off before the trigger
is live: it plays 851-1034 ms of the sniper's 1250, against a
`cycle.tiltOut[1]` of 0.96 that finishes the picture at 1200. The rifle is
quiet, still and loaded for the last 216 ms of every cycle, which is the
claim the reload's fourth beat already makes at 0.8.
